bill.name: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Department of Energy relating to “Energy Conservation Program for Appliance Standards: Certification Requirements, Labeling Requirements, and Enforcement Provisions for Certain Consumer Products and Commercial Equipment” (H.J. Res. 42)
bill.status: Became Public Law 119-8 on 2025-05-09 · introduced-in-House source submitted by Clyde and referred to Energy and Commerce on 2025-02-12
bill.analyzed: Full introduced-in-House joint resolution (two pages; one operative clause), with enacted disposition checked separately

provisions.title: H.J. Res. 42
provisions.heading: Congressional disapproval of the identified DOE appliance-standards certification, labeling, and enforcement rule
provisions.quote: That Congress disapproves the rule submitted by the Department of Energy relating to Energy Conservation Program for Appliance Standards: Certification Requirements, Labeling Requirements, and Enforcement Provisions for Certain Consumer Products and Commercial Equipment (89 Fed. Reg. 81994 (October 9, 2024)), and such rule shall have no force or effect.
provisions.context:
H.J. Res. 42 invokes chapter 8 of title 5 and identifies one Department of Energy rule by title and Federal Register citation. Mr. Clyde submitted the analyzed introduced-in-House version on February 12, 2025; it was referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce. Its sole operative clause states that Congress disapproves the cited rule and that the rule shall have no force or effect. Congress.gov separately records that the measure became Public Law 119-8 on May 9, 2025, so the enactment contingency presented by the analyzed version was later satisfied.

Source limits / honesty note: The supplied flattened text identifies the rule but does not reproduce it, state its requirements, articulate findings or a purpose beyond disapproval, specify transition or implementation steps, or identify a quantitative outcome. The matching official introduced-version PDF establishes pagination at two pages, but the flat extraction omits page boundaries and the standard resolving formula. Congress.gov disposition metadata, not the supplied raw text, establishes enactment. This analysis therefore records only the express legal objective and effect plus that separately verified disposition. It makes no claims about covered products or equipment, certification or labeling requirements, enforcement activity, energy use or savings, compliance costs, regulated entities, agency behavior, successor-rule constraints, or the post-disapproval regulatory baseline. It has zero forecastable metrics, series hints, stance matrices, or empirical conditionals.
goals: Disapprove the identified Department of Energy rule so that it has no force or effect.

effects.text: On enactment, H.J. Res. 42 disapproved the Department of Energy rule cited at 89 Fed. Reg. 81994 and provided that it has no force or effect; Congress.gov records approval as Public Law 119-8 on May 9, 2025.
